name: Quadratic assignment, QAPLIB tho40
description: Quadratic assignment problem, QAPLIB instance tho40: given two 40 x 40 integer matrices a and b, find a permutation p of 0..39 that minimises the cost, the sum over all i and j of a[i, j] * b[p[i], p[j]]. In the usual reading one matrix holds the flows between facilities and the other the distances between locations, and p assigns the one to the other; the cost formula is what is scored.

execution.interface: solve(a, b) -> permutation p of 0..n-1 (a list of n integers, each exactly once). a and b are the first and second matrix of the QAPLIB file (int64 arrays of shape (n, n), passed as copies). Score: the exact integer cost, the sum over all i and j of a[i, j] * b[p[i], p[j]], minimized.

science_relevance.reason: Koopmans and Beckmann pose the quadratic assignment problem, and the group papers listed per instance are the ones QAPLIB credits with the instance set or its best known solution; all have the problem itself as their main objective, and the evaluator scores exactly the QAP cost of a permutation on the pinned QAPLIB instance.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a minimum-cost Koopmans-Beckmann quadratic assignment of 40 facilities to 40 locations for the QAPLIB instance tho40, which is not solved to optimality.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The quadratic assignment problem models facility and hospital layout, keyboard design, backboard wiring and the generation of grey patterns. It is NP-hard and hard in practice: QAPLIB instances above about 30 facilities are mostly unsolved, and the best known solutions of the larger ones have stood for many years, so a cheaper permutation is a new best known solution of a standard open instance.
